tagline: Coal-country highways under the title of a 1908 bestseller.
intro: From Bluefield, US 19 and US 460 follow the Clinch River and the Clinch Valley rail line through Pounding Mill, and on toward Lebanon US 19 carries the title of John Fox Jr.'s 1908 novel. Farther west the road reaches St. Paul, begun in 1791 as a Huguenot settlement above the Clinch, then Coeburn, Norton and Big Stone Gap.

From there the web spreads out. Route 70 heads south from Jonesville over Powell Mountain on the old Trail of the Lonesome Pine auto trail from Detroit to Florida. US 23 runs north through Wise to Pound Gap, and Route 160 climbs out of Appalachia on hairpin turns to Black Mountain at the Kentucky line.

moments.title: Norton
moments.text: Once called Prince's Flats, the town took the name of the Louisville and Nashville's president in a bid for a depot, and is now the least populous city in Virginia.

moments.title: John Fox Jr. House
moments.text: Fox wrote The Trail of the Lonesome Pine in this house on Shawnee Avenue, and June Morris, who boarded in town while at school, became its heroine June Tolliver.

moments.title: Pound Gap
moments.text: US 23 crosses Pine Mountain into Kentucky through the gap Daniel Boone called Sounding Gap, where early families of eastern Kentucky came through about 1800.

practical: Route 160 between Appalachia and Lynch, Kentucky is signposted closed to tractor-trailers because of its tight bends.
